title: Kerala - Best Time to Visit, Top Destinations & Travel Tips
content:
Kerala - God’s Own Country

Kerala, often called “God’s Own Country”, is one of the most beautiful states in India. Located in the southern part of the country, Kerala is famous for its stunning backwaters, lush green landscapes, beaches, wildlife, Ayurveda, and rich culture. It is a perfect travel destination for nature lovers, adventure seekers, and those looking for peace and relaxation.

Kerala is one of the top travel destinations in India, offering a mix of natural beauty, wellness, and cultural richness. 

Click here for Travel Packages

Here are some strong reasons why you must visit Kerala at least once in your lifetime:

  • Backwaters & Houseboats - A ride through Kerala’s backwaters in Alleppey or Kumarakom is a magical experience. Staying in a traditional houseboat while watching the sunset over palm-fringed waters is unforgettable.
  • Stunning Beaches - Kerala has some of the cleanest and most beautiful beaches in India. Kovalam, Varkala, Marari, and Bekal are perfect for sunbathing, swimming, and water sports.
  • Hill Stations & Tea Plantations - Munnar, Wayanad, and Vagamon are breathtaking hill stations covered with tea and spice plantations, waterfalls, and misty mountains. A great escape for honeymooners and nature lovers.
  • Ayurveda & Wellness Tourism - Kerala is world-famous for its Ayurvedic treatments, yoga, and wellness retreats. Tourists from across the globe come here for relaxation, healing, and rejuvenation.
  • Rich Culture & Traditions - Festivals like Onam and Thrissur Pooram, and art forms like Kathakali, Theyyam, and Mohiniyattam, showcase Kerala’s vibrant heritage. The temples, churches, and mosques here reflect centuries of tradition.
  • Wildlife & Adventure - Kerala is home to rich wildlife sanctuaries like Periyar, Silent Valley, and Eravikulam National Park, where you can spot elephants, tigers, and rare birds. Adventure lovers can enjoy trekking, bamboo rafting, and jungle camping.
  • Delicious Cuisine - Kerala food is a treat for your taste buds. From the grand Onam Sadhya served on a banana leaf to seafood delicacies like Karimeen Pollichathu and Fish Curry, every dish is full of flavor.
  • Serenity & Natural Beauty - With coconut palms, paddy fields, rivers, and waterfalls, Kerala is blessed with a peaceful charm. It’s the perfect destination for those who want to disconnect from city life and enjoy pure nature.

List of the top tourist places in Kerala:

1. Alleppey (Alappuzha) “The Backwater Paradise”- Famous for: Houseboat cruises, backwaters, Vembanad Lake. Must-do: Stay in a houseboat, explore Kuttanad.
2. Munnar “The Green Hill Station”: Famous for- Tea plantations, cool climate, scenic valleys. Must-see: Eravikulam National Park, Tea Museum, Mattupetty Dam.
3. Kochi (Cochin) “The Queen of the Arabian Sea”-  Famous for: Colonial heritage, spice markets, Chinese fishing nets. Must-see: Fort Kochi, Mattancherry Palace, Jew Street.
4. Thekkady “Wildlife and Spice Capital”- Famous for: Periyar Wildlife Sanctuary. Must-do: Boat ride on Periyar Lake, spice plantation tours.
5. Wayanad “Nature and Adventure”- Famous for: Waterfalls, caves, wildlife sanctuaries. Must-see: Edakkal Caves, Banasura Sagar Dam, Soochipara Falls.
6. Kovalam “Beach Destination”- Famous for: Crescent-shaped beaches, lighthouses. Must-do: Surfing, sunbathing, Ayurvedic treatments.
7. Kumarakom “Serene Backwaters”- Famous for: Bird sanctuary, houseboat cruises. Must-see: Vembanad Lake, Kumarakom Bird Sanctuary.
8. Thiruvananthapuram (Trivandrum) “Capital City with a Spiritual Vibe”- Famous for: Padmanabhaswamy Temple, museums, beaches. Must-see: Kovalam Beach, Napier Museum, Poovar Island.
9. Varkala “Cliffs and Spirituality”- Famous for: Cliff-side beach views, pilgrimage sites. Must-see: Varkala Beach, Janardana Swami Temple.
10. Athirappilly “The Niagara of India”- Famous for: Athirappilly and Vazhachal waterfalls. Nearby: Sholayar Forests, wildlife watching. 

Best Time to Visit Kerala

Winter (October to February): The most pleasant season, perfect for sightseeing and backwater cruises.
Monsoon (June to September): Ideal for Ayurvedic treatments and enjoying the lush greenery.
Summer (March to May): Hot but still beautiful, especially in hill stations like Munnar.

Travel Tips for Kerala

Carry light cotton clothes.
Don’t miss an Ayurvedic massage.
Try local dishes like Appam, Puttu, and Kerala Sadhya.
Respect local traditions and dress modestly at temples.
excerpt: Kerala is truly a paradise where you can enjoy nature, culture, and wellness all in one place. Whether it’s a relaxing houseboat ride, a walk through tea plantations, or a rejuvenating Ayurvedic therapy, Kerala promises an unforgettable experience.

faqs.question: Which are the top tourist places in Kerala?
faqs.answer:
Q8. Which are the top tourist places in Kerala?
The top tourist destinations are Alleppey, Munnar, Wayanad, Kumarakom, Kochi, Kovalam, Varkala, and Thekkady.

faqs.question: What are the must-try foods in Kerala?
faqs.answer: Some must-try dishes are Appam with Stew, Kerala Fish Curry, Karimeen Pollichathu, Puttu and Kadala Curry, Malabar Parotta, and Kerala Sadhya.

faqs.question: How many days are enough to explore Kerala?
faqs.answer: A trip of 7 to 10 days is ideal to cover major attractions like Munnar, Alleppey, Kochi, Thekkady, and Wayanad. However, shorter trips of 4–5 days are also possible for quick getaways.

faqs.question: Is Kerala good for a honeymoon?
faqs.answer: Yes! Kerala is one of the most romantic honeymoon destinations in India. Hill stations like Munnar, backwaters in Alleppey, and beaches in Kovalam offer couples a perfect blend of relaxation and romance.

faqs.question: What is Kerala famous for?
faqs.answer: Kerala is famous for its backwaters, Ayurveda treatments, Kathakali dance, tea plantations, houseboats, delicious seafood, and vibrant festivals like Onam.

faqs.question: Which is the best time to visit Kerala?
faqs.answer: The best time to visit Kerala is October to February when the weather is pleasant for sightseeing and backwater cruises. However, the monsoon season (June–September) is perfect for Ayurvedic treatments and enjoying lush greenery.
